events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents Takeo Moriyama 2DAYS on Friday, September 11 and Saturday, September 12, 2026. Doors are at 7:00 PM and both performances begin at 7:30 PM. The announced quintet is Takeo Moriyama on drums, Tetsuro Kawashima on tenor saxophone, Takumi Nakayama on alto saxophone, Reiko Yamamoto on vibraphone, and Takashi Sugawa on bass. PIT INN publishes admission at ¥5,500 including one drink and states that advance reservations are available at the venue counter, by phone, or through each performance's reservation form.

en.why_it_matters: The current quintet is the reason, not Moriyama's history alone: twin saxophones and vibraphone sit over Sugawa's bass and Moriyama's drums, giving one of the defining drummers of Japan's post-1960s jazz lineage a colorful present-tense small-group sound at PIT INN. The instrumentation also echoes the reed-and-rhythm openness long associated with Moriyama without pretending this is a retrospective program.
en.trip_verdict: If September 11-12 overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for one night and let Shinjuku anchor the evening. Two performances provide flexibility, so this belongs as a strong Tokyo priority rather than a reason by itself to restructure the wider Japan trip.

es.why_it_matters: La razón es el quinteto actual, no sólo la historia de Moriyama: dos saxofones y vibráfono se apoyan sobre el bajo de Sugawa y la batería de Moriyama, dándole a uno de los bateristas definitorios del jazz japonés posterior a los sesenta un sonido de grupo pequeño, vivo y actual, en PIT INN. La instrumentación además conversa con la apertura de alientos y ritmo asociada desde hace décadas con Moriyama sin fingir que se trata de un programa retrospectivo.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 11 o 12 de septiembre coincide con una estancia en Tokio, le haría espacio activamente a una noche y dejaría que Shinjuku ancle la velada. Tener dos funciones da flexibilidad, así que funciona como una prioridad fuerte dentro de Tokio y no como motivo único para reestructurar todo el viaje a Japón.

events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents Marsalis’ Swinging Cities at Rose Theater on Friday, November 6 and Saturday, November 7, 2026, at 7:30 PM, with a 6:30 PM pre-concert lecture each night. The Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis performs music from Vitoria Suite, Shanghai Suite, and Marciac Suite in a program JALC describes as reflecting cultures, experiences, places, and relationships accumulated across Marsalis's decades of touring. The engagement falls in Marsalis's 2026-27 final season as Artistic Director of Jazz at Lincoln Center.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the repertoire arc, not Marsalis's stature alone: Vitoria Suite, Shanghai Suite and Marciac Suite turn three places and decades of touring relationships into one orchestral argument about how jazz absorbs and answers local culture. In his final season as JALC Artistic Director, that makes the program a focused institutional self-portrait rather than another prestige orchestra date.
en.trip_verdict: If New York already makes sense that weekend, catch one of the two nights and pair Rose Theater with another reason to be in the city. The program is worth knowing and attending when convenient, but two performances and a full Marsalis-centered season mean it does not need to dictate a corridor trip on its own.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho es el arco de repertorio, no sólo el peso del nombre de Marsalis: Vitoria Suite, Shanghai Suite y Marciac Suite convierten tres lugares y décadas de relaciones construidas en gira en un argumento orquestal sobre cómo el jazz absorbe y responde a la cultura local. En su última temporada como director artístico de JALC, el programa funciona como un autorretrato institucional concentrado y no como otra fecha de prestigio de una gran orquesta.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya hace sentido ese fin de semana, escogería una de las dos noches y combinaría Rose Theater con otra razón para estar en la ciudad. Vale la pena conocerla y aprovecharla si embona, pero dos funciones y una temporada entera centrada en Marsalis hacen que no deba dictar por sí sola un viaje por el corredor.
